title: Harissa Halloumi, Sweet Potato & Kale Salad
style: Warm sheet-pan salad — roasted sweet potato and crispy chickpeas over massaged kale, golden halloumi, and a sweet-hot harissa tahini dressing
description: Roasted sweet potato and chickpeas piled onto kale massaged with harissa tahini, topped with pan-fried halloumi. Warm, substantial, and about 22 g protein per serving.

items.note: 400–425 g, drained, rinsed and rubbed dry
ribs and stems removed, chopped — about 5 heaping cups
heat varies wildly by brand — start low

steps: Prep: Heat the oven to 220°C / 425°F. After draining and rinsing the chickpeas, rub them between a clean tea towel to dry them thoroughly and shed the loose skins — wet chickpeas steam instead of crisping.

Sheet pan: Tip the chickpeas and cubed sweet potato onto a large baking sheet, drizzle with the olive oil, and season with salt and pepper. Toss to coat, then spread out in a single layer with nothing overlapping.
Roast for 25 minutes, until the sweet potato is tender and the chickpeas have crisped up. Let cool slightly.
Halloumi: Meanwhile, bring a non-stick pan to medium heat. Fry the halloumi slices until golden, about 2–3 minutes per side, then set aside.
Dressing: Combine the tahini, harissa, maple syrup, lemon juice, water, and salt in a jar and shake, or stir in a small bowl. Adjust the water to get a pourable consistency — it thickens as it sits.
Massage the kale: Put the chopped kale in a large bowl, pour over most of the dressing, holding some back, and work it into the leaves with your hands until they soften and darken.
Top the kale with the roasted sweet potato and chickpeas, then the halloumi, and spoon over the remaining dressing. Garnish with parsley and serve warm.
tips: This lands as a lightly dressed salad. If you like things wetter, double every dressing ingredient — it's the change most people want on the second make.
Harissa heat is wildly inconsistent between brands. Start at half a tablespoon, taste, and climb from there rather than committing up front.
Massaging the kale isn't optional theatre — it breaks down the tough cell walls so lacinato goes tender instead of squeaky.
Dry the chickpeas properly before they hit the oil. It's the single biggest factor in whether they crisp or go leathery.
Halloumi is at its best straight out of the pan; it turns squeaky and firm as it cools, so fry it last and assemble immediately.
For a no-oven summer version of the same flavours, see the Charred Halloumi & Crispy Chickpea Salad instead.
